title: AI in Excel 1: built-in AI and Copilot

questions.question: You have a column of full names and want first names only, by typing one example and letting Excel follow the pattern. Which built-in tool fits this job?

answerOptions.text: Analyze Data
answerOptions.rationale: Analyze Data answers questions about numbers in a table; it does not split text.

answerOptions.text: Flash Fill
answerOptions.rationale: Flash Fill copies a pattern from an example you type, with no licence or prompt needed.

answerOptions.text: Copilot advanced analysis with Python
answerOptions.rationale: Python forecasting and clustering is far more than this simple pattern job needs.

answerOptions.text: Plan mode
answerOptions.rationale: Plan mode is for reviewing multi-step Copilot edits, not a one-column text pattern.

questions.question: Analyze Data says it cannot find patterns in your sheet. What should you check first?

answerOptions.text: Blank rows in the middle and merged header cells; keep one clear header row
answerOptions.rationale: Analyze Data needs one tidy table, and blank rows or merged headers break it.

answerOptions.text: Whether you have a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence
answerOptions.rationale: Analyze Data comes with Microsoft 365 and does not need a Copilot licence.

answerOptions.text: Whether the file is protected with a password
answerOptions.rationale: The lesson points to layout problems, not passwords.

answerOptions.text: Whether Claude in Excel is installed
answerOptions.rationale: Analyze Data is built in and does not depend on any add-in.

questions.question: On Excel for Mac, the Copilot button is greyed out and the AutoSave switch at the top left is off. What is the most likely cause?

answerOptions.text: The data has too many rows for Copilot
answerOptions.rationale: Row count is not one of the checklist causes for a greyed-out button.

answerOptions.text: Gridlines are switched off
answerOptions.rationale: Gridlines have no effect on Copilot.

answerOptions.text: The file is saved only on your Mac, not on OneDrive or SharePoint
answerOptions.rationale: Copilot needs the file on OneDrive or SharePoint with AutoSave on.

answerOptions.text: The sheet has a PivotTable on it
answerOptions.rationale: PivotTables do not disable Copilot.

questions.question: What can Copilot do in Chat mode?

answerOptions.text: Add formula columns directly to the table
answerOptions.rationale: Adding columns is an Edit mode job.

answerOptions.text: Build a full dashboard on a new sheet by itself
answerOptions.rationale: Multi-step builds are done in Edit (Agent) mode.

answerOptions.text: Run only when the file is saved on your Mac
answerOptions.rationale: All Copilot modes need the file on OneDrive or SharePoint, not local only.

answerOptions.text: Read the data and answer questions, without changing the sheet
answerOptions.rationale: Chat mode reads and answers; nothing on the sheet changes.

questions.question: Copilot has just added an Amount column with a formula. What should you do before trusting it?

answerOptions.text: Nothing; formulas written by Copilot cannot be wrong
answerOptions.rationale: The lesson warns it can pick the wrong column, such as Unit price instead of Amount.

answerOptions.text: Click the first result cell, read the formula bar and check one row by hand
answerOptions.rationale: Copilot can pick the wrong column when headers sound alike, so read and check.

answerOptions.text: Delete the column and type it yourself every time
answerOptions.rationale: The formula is a normal Excel formula; you read and check it rather than discard it.

answerOptions.text: Ask Copilot the same question again and accept it if the answer repeats
answerOptions.rationale: A repeated answer is not a check; your own one-row calculation is.

questions.question: You added new rows to the source data, but the PivotTable Copilot built still shows the old totals. What do you do?

answerOptions.text: Click inside the PivotTable and Refresh it
answerOptions.rationale: PivotTables do not update by themselves; Refresh pulls in the new rows.

answerOptions.text: Ask Copilot to build a new PivotTable each time
answerOptions.rationale: That works but is unnecessary; a Refresh is enough.

answerOptions.text: Turn AutoSave off and on again
answerOptions.rationale: AutoSave saves the file; it does not refresh PivotTables.

answerOptions.text: Press Command Z
answerOptions.rationale: Undo would reverse your last change, not refresh the PivotTable.

questions.question: A ticket dated 03/04/2025 (written the Indian way) shows as 4 March 2025 after Copilot converts the dates. What happened, and what is the fix?

answerOptions.text: The date is correct; Excel always stores dates month first
answerOptions.rationale: The ticket meant 3 April, so 4 March is wrong.

answerOptions.text: The cell needs a wider column
answerOptions.rationale: Column width changes the display, not which day and month were read.

answerOptions.text: Copilot read it as month first; undo with Command Z and repeat that the dates are day first
answerOptions.rationale: In India 03/04 means 3 April, so tell Copilot the dates are day first.

answerOptions.text: Use the =COPILOT() function instead
answerOptions.rationale: =COPILOT() was retired on 14 September 2026; the pane does these jobs now.

questions.question: Which set of parts makes a good spreadsheet prompt, as taught in this section?

answerOptions.text: A greeting, the file name and a thank-you
answerOptions.rationale: Politeness does not tell Copilot what to do with the data.

answerOptions.text: Only the goal, kept as short as possible
answerOptions.rationale: A vague prompt like "tell me about this data" gets a generic answer.

answerOptions.text: The full data pasted into the prompt
answerOptions.rationale: Copilot already reads the sheet; name the columns instead of pasting data.

answerOptions.text: Goal, data, output and constraints
answerOptions.rationale: Saying what you want, which columns, the form of the answer and any rules gives specific results.
